title: Probation Prep Pack
description: The composite pack for the final twenty-one days before your probation review. Self-assessment template + pre-review 1:1 agenda + evidence portfolio + the conversation itself, all aligned to a single review date.
empty_template_md:
## Probation Prep Pack — [name]

**Review date:** [date]
**Manager:** [name]

### 1. Self-assessment (one page)

Three paragraphs, no more.

**Delivered.** _What I have actually done in 90 days, with the receipts. Specific. Not adjective-heavy._

**Learned.** _What I learned that I didn't know on Day 1. Be honest about misjudgements; show what changed._

**Want next.** _What I'd like to focus on in the next 90 days, with one specific thing I want from my manager to make it possible._

### 2. Pre-review 1:1 agenda (15 minutes, 5-7 days before the review)

This is the meeting where you de-risk the review meeting.

- _Ask: are there any concerns I haven't heard about yet?_
- _Share your self-assessment in advance; ask whether the framing matches their read._
- _Surface anything you already know is a soft spot — own it first._

### 3. Evidence portfolio

Three pieces of work. For each:

- **What it was:** one sentence.
- **What I did:** one paragraph; specific verbs.
- **What changed because of it:** one sentence; outcome, not effort.
- **What I'd do differently:** one sentence; honest.

Keep file links, dates, named (anonymised) collaborators. Make it scannable.

### 4. The review conversation

Go in with:
- A printed copy of your self-assessment + portfolio.
- One question you want them to answer (e.g., "what's the one thing you'd want to see different in the next 90 days?").
- A note-taking pad.

Leave with:
- A clear yes / no / extended on probation.
- Two or three specific notes — what they liked, what they want different.
- A written summary you send within 24 hours.

worked_examples.title: Worked example — BA, day 87
worked_examples.content_md:
## My probation prep pack — day 87 of 90

**Review date:** Wednesday next week.
**Manager:** Bea Connors.

### 1. Self-assessment

**Delivered.** In 12 weeks I have written 2 BRDs (partner-portal + expense-tool migration), 23 user stories with acceptance criteria, and run 4 requirements workshops as primary facilitator. I held the room in the defect-triage meeting that the team had been dreading, and surfaced the de-scoping email that reframed three defects. The partner-portal launches on schedule on Thursday.

**Learned.** I came in over-indexed on the BRD as the central artefact. Eight weeks in I realised the stakeholder map was doing more work than any BRD, because it explained why every meeting went the way it did. I also misjudged when to escalate the compliance concern in week 11 — I should have called Marcus on Tuesday, not waited until Wednesday morning. That's the moment I most want to do differently.

**Want next.** In the next 90 days I want to lead a piece of work end-to-end where Bea is observing rather than guiding. Specifically: the partner-onboarding process redesign that's lined up for Q2. I'd like Bea to be the second BA on the project — present but not driving.

### 2. Pre-review 1:1

Booked for Monday, 5 days before the review. Agenda:
- I'm sharing this self-assessment now. Does the framing match your read?
- Specifically: I know the way I communicated the week-7 slip wasn't great. I've thought about what I'd do differently — I'd like to talk about whether what I've worked out matches what you'd want.
- Is there anything you'd want to flag now that you'd rather not surface in the review meeting itself?

### 3. Evidence portfolio

**Partner-portal BRD (week 4).** I wrote the BRD that anchored the partner-portal initiative across 3 stakeholders with conflicting positions. The de-scoping email I prepared in week 5 was referenced 6 weeks later to reset the defect-triage meeting (week 11). What I'd do differently: I'd write the out-of-scope section first, not last — the conversations that matter happened around what wasn't included.

**Defect-triage in week 11.** Facilitated a 60-minute meeting where the PO and lead engineer were openly blaming each other for the UAT defect list. I triaged the list by category (bugs / requirement gaps / de-scoped items) and surfaced the de-scoping email. The meeting closed with every defect owned and categorised; the team avoided the week of recriminations that would otherwise have happened. What I'd do differently: I'd have established the categorisation framework in week 1, not week 11 — the same defect-triage exercise on a smaller project would have built the muscle.

**Compliance escalation in week 11.** Marcus surfaced a concern 48 hours before launch. I called rather than emailed, caught the "three other places" remark, and triggered the end-of-day sweep that fixed all four issues before Thursday morning. What I'd do differently: I'd not have waited the half-day before calling him. The email landed at 11am. I called at 3pm. I should have called at 11:15.

### 4. The review conversation

Going in with the printed pack + this question for Bea: "If you could choose only one thing I work on in the next 90 days, what would it be?"

If the answer is anything other than "keep doing what you're doing" — which it won't be — that becomes the focal point of my next 90-day plan.

annotations.note: Three short paragraphs is the discipline. Probation self-assessments that run to four pages of adjectives are not read; one page of specifics is.
The "Learned" paragraph is the one that decides probation reviews. Honest learning shows judgement; defensive learning shows the opposite.
The "want next" line ends with a specific ask of the manager. "I'd like Bea to be the second BA on Q2" beats "I'd like more autonomy" every time.
The pre-review meeting is where you flush surprises out. Anything you discover in this meeting is something you don't have to discover in the review meeting itself.
Each portfolio entry has a "what I'd do differently" line. Without it, the pack reads as a victory lap. With it, it reads as someone who's still learning.

common_mistakes: Writing a self-assessment of three pages instead of three paragraphs. Length signals anxiety, not depth. Cut.
Skipping the pre-review meeting because "the review is in 5 days anyway". The pre-review is what makes the review boring — which is exactly what you want.
Portfolios that record effort rather than outcome. "Spent 40 hours on the BRD" is not evidence. "BRD shipped, anchored the de-scoping decision in week 11" is.
Walking out of the review with vague encouragement and no written summary. If you can't write the five-sentence summary that night, you didn't have the conversation that needed having.
variant_patterns: Probation extended variant: the conversation about an extended probation needs the same structure but with explicit milestones for the extension period (what changes, what gets reviewed, by when).
Probation passed-with-concerns variant: leave the meeting with the concerns written down and a follow-up booked. "Passed with concerns" is two months of unfinished business if you don't formalise it.
